decisions.reason: Removing visible Heyzine branding does not change the required page format, even page count, or two-page spread behavior.
The white-label preference changes the platform-branding workflow, not the requirement to deliver an interactive PDF for the digital flipbook.
The branding decision does not alter article-ending white-space rules; the independent image-filler clause from the same message is already represented in this Requirement.
Flipbook platform branding has no effect on the issue month or inaugural-edition label.
A white-label flipbook presentation does not change the requirement for accurate article page numbers on the cover.
The removal of visible Heyzine branding does not change the table-of-contents completion condition or page-number basis.
Platform white-label branding is unrelated to advertisement clarity, resolution, trim, or bleed quality.

The candidate governs the magazine layout's Civic Lantern visual identity, while the source decision concerns suppression of the hosting platform's Heyzine branding; its existing attributes remain valid unchanged.
The platform-branding preference does not change the requirement to enhance low-quality publication images when necessary.
The template remains required and completed; the separate white-label request does not modify template creation state.
Heyzine branding does not affect author names, photographs, sources, or placement on article pages.
White-label presentation does not change the reported contents-to-chapter and return-link navigation behavior.
